meta.methodology: Read framework.md, torah_74_packages.json, all reference===74 edges from torahData.js, and the full source text torah_74.txt (both the original short version and Natan Sternhartz's expanded version). For each bechina statement in the source text, verified whether the concept appears as a node in the dataset for reference===74. Only concepts with explicit bechina language (בְּחִינַת, הַיְנוּ, נִקְרָא, הוּא [as equivalence declaration]) were considered. Narrative descriptions, proof-text citations without conceptual declaration, causal explanations (eitza), and standard Talmudic equivalences used only as supporting quotes were excluded from flagging.

additions.reason: The concept מֹחִין דְּקַטְנוּת is used with explicit bechina language repeatedly throughout Torah #74 and is in fact one of the two defining poles of the entire teaching (katnut vs. gadlut). Lines 5 (original), 30, 33, 34 all use בְּחִינַת to equate the holy judgment / initial state of distancing with מֹחִין דְּקַטְנוּת. Specifically: 'הוּא בְּחִינַת מֹחִין דְּקַטְנוּת' (lines 5, 30), 'הַדִּינִים הֵם מִבְּחִינַת מֹחִין דְּקַטְנוּת' (line 33), 'אָז הוּא בְּחִינַת מֹחִין דְּקַטְנוּת' (line 34). The dataset contains edges for מחין דקטנות in other Torahs (ref 46, 76, 234) but ZERO edges for reference===74. This is a critical gap: without מחין דקטנות in the Torah 74 graph, the connection between the דין/יצחק cluster (Package 1) and its psychological/spiritual nature as contracted consciousness is absent. Polarity neutral because מחין דקטנות is a structural state — the moon-state of Isaac — not inherently evil (it is the valid starting point of every spiritual journey) but also not inherently good.
additions.source_quote: הוּא בְּחִינַת מֹחִין דְּקַטְנוּת, שֶׁמִּשָּׁם עִקַּר אֲחִיזַת הַדִּין

suggested_edges.proof: דִּין הַקָּדוֹשׁ, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת יִצְחָק...הוּא בְּחִינַת מֹחִין דְּקַטְנוּת
כְּשֶׁהַמַּלְכוּת הִיא בִּבְחִינַת צֶדֶק, אָז הוּא בְּחִינַת מֹחִין דְּקַטְנוּת

additions.reason: The concept צֶדֶק receives multiple explicit נִקְרָא bechina declarations in Torah #74, making it a named bechina aspect of the judgment-katnut domain. Line 6 (original): 'וְהַמַּלְכוּת נִקְרָא צֶדֶק' (Malkhut is called Tzedek when in the katnut/din state). Line 17: 'וְהַדִּבּוּר בְּלֹא דֵּעָה נִקְרָא צֶדֶק' (speech-without-knowledge is called Tzedek). Line 34: 'שֶׁאָז נִקְרֵאת הַמַּלְכוּת צֶדֶק כַּיָּדוּעַ'. Line 47: 'כִּי כְּשֶׁהַמַּלְכוּת בִּבְחִינַת דִּין, נִקְרֵאת צֶדֶק'. Tzedek is the name of Malkhut in her contracted/judgment state (as distinct from Tzedakah, which is her name after sweetening/elevation through Yaakov/wisdom). This is a central conceptual pair in Torah #74: צֶדֶק → צְדָקָה = the journey from katnut to gadlut. The dataset has edge 666 for צדקה ↔ דבור בדעה but NO edge defining צדק as a Torah-74 bechina. Polarity neutral because צדק is the name for Malkhut in its valid din-state — not evil, but the neutral form of judgment before sweetening.

Note: this proposed addition concerns the BECHINA EDGE תורה ↔ חכמה for reference 74, not a new node (both תורה and חכמה are already in Package 2). The gap is a missing edge connecting them.

The אור/חשך duality is structurally important as the light-metaphor bridge between Packages 1 and 2. concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Lines 29-30 use בְּחִינַת to connect the state of distancing with the beginning of drawing near: 'זֶהוּ בְּחִינַת הִתְרַחֲקוּת, שֶׁהוּא הַתְחָלַת הַהִתְקָרְבוּת'. However, this is a causal/consequential relationship stated in descriptive language about what the dinim look like (they look like distancing but are really drawing-near). The בְּחִינַת here modifies הִתְרַחֲקוּת as a metaphor/appearance ('it appears as distancing') rather than declaring a bechina equivalence between two concepts. Excluded as eitza/descriptive language.

Line 15 mentions God forming Isaac's facial features to look like Abraham's (כְּלַסְתֵּר פָּנִים). This is narrative detail supporting the teaching's argument about the holy judgment's origin from chesed. It is not a bechina equivalence statement — the Rebbe does not say 'klaster panim IS a bechina of X'. Excluded as narrative/proof-story.

Line 49: 'יִשְׂרָאֵל עָלוּ בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה תְּחִלָּה' — 'Israel arose in divine thought first.' This is used to explain why machshava/chokhmah is the root of souls, not to establish a bechina equivalence for Israel as a concept. The Rebbe does not say 'Israel IS a bechina of chokhmah'; rather, Israel's origin is within chokhmah. Excluded as supporting citation rather than bechina declaration.

Lines 19, 49: 'טִפַּת הַזֶּרַע נִמְשֶׁכֶת מֵהַמֹּחַ' — the seed-drop is drawn FROM the brain. This is an eitza relationship (the brain produces the seed-drop), not a bechina equation. The seed-drop is used to illustrate why the soul can be elevated to its root through wisdom (chokhmah/mochin). The concept itself is not declared as a bechina of another concept. Excluded as eitza.

Line 50: 'זֶהוּ בְּחִינַת חִדּוּשׁ הָעוֹלָם' — 'this IS the bechina of the renewal of the world.' The Rebbe uses בְּחִינַת here to say that when a soul attains Torah-wisdom, THIS IS the renewal of the world. However, the subject is the spiritual achievement (reaching chokhmah), and חדוש העולם is presented as its consequence/result — which is more characteristic of an eitza-outcome than a bechina-equivalence. Furthermore, the Rebbe's use of בְּחִינַת here means 'this is equivalent to' in a metaphorical sense (similar to: 'this is tantamount to the renewal of the world'), not that two concepts are structurally parallel aspects of the same thing. Borderline case; excluded to avoid over-extraction.

Line 12 / line 46: 'שֶׁמֶשׁ וּמָגֵן ה' אֱלֹקִים — h' אֱלֹקִים, זֶה בְּחִינַת רַחֲמִים וְדִין, בְּחִינַת יַעֲקֹב וְיִצְחָק, שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת שֶׁמֶשׁ וּמָגֵן'. The verse 'shemesh u'magen' is interpreted: shemesh = Yaakov; magen = Yitzchak. The בְּחִינַת here could imply מָגֵן = יצחק = דין. However, the dataset already captures לבנה ↔ יצחק and יצחק ↔ דין — the shield/protection metaphor is implicit in the moon-and-din cluster. The explicit equation מָגֵן = יצחק is not stated directly with a נִקְרָא or הוּא formula; it is derived from the verse's structure. Borderline; excluded to avoid implicit-inference additions.

Lines 14, 37: 'הִסְתַּרְתָּ פָנֶיךָ הָיִיתִי נִבְהָל' is interpreted as the state when תְּפִלָּה is cancelled (ביטול תפלה). The 'hiding of the face' is presented as an extreme negative state contrasted with the normal תפלה/פנים state. However, הסתרת פנים is not declared as a bechina equivalence to another concept in Torah 74 — it is used as a descriptive contrast ('when prayer is cancelled, it is like/is the hiding of the face'). The concept is the negative form of the פנים/תפלה pair already in the dataset (Package 1). Excluded as descriptive contrast rather than bechina equivalence. If added, it would be a new edge: הסתרת פנים ↔ ביטול תפלה (which is also possible), but the text reads more descriptively than declaratively here.

analysis_notes.most_critical_gap: מחין דקטנות — this is the name for the state of Isaac/Hoshana Rabba/din in Torah 74 and is mentioned with bechina language at least 4 times, but has ZERO edges in the Torah 74 dataset. Its absence means the graph misses the core ontological label for the katnut pole of the teaching.
